subject.title: MEDIA: tokens inside markdown code fences are silently ignored

question: Should fenced legacy `MEDIA:` directives remain non-extracting with warn-only diagnostics, be extracted as attachments, or stay documented as by-design only?
rationale: Current code intentionally preserves fenced examples as text, but the reported silent failure affects real attachment delivery; extraction versus diagnostics changes the product contract and false-positive risk.

options.title: Warn Only At Delivery Boundary
options.body: Keep fenced tokens as text, emit one diagnostic warning in the real outbound delivery path, and land the linked PR after the remaining warning-path repair.

options.title: Extract Standalone Fenced Tokens
options.body: Treat standalone fenced `MEDIA:` lines as attachments, accepting that code examples may become deliverable media unless a stricter policy is designed.

options.title: Docs Only
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and rely on docs and prompts that legacy `MEDIA:` lines must be standalone plain text.

recommendation.title: Warn Only At Delivery Boundary
recommendation.body: Keep fenced tokens as text, emit one diagnostic warning in the real outbound delivery path, and land the linked PR after the remaining warning-path repair.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has current blame on the parser/test contract and the live review specifying the delivery-boundary warning direction on the linked PR.
